literal: Zhang Qiong, styled Liande, was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Zhang Qiong, styled Liande, was a native of Dai.

literal: In youth he was strong and robust, and possessed martial ability.
idiomatic: In youth he was strong and robust, and possessed martial ability.

literal: During the Wei era he rose from General Who Sweeps Bandits to outside-military military assistant in the expeditionary office of Shuo Province, and followed Ge Rong in rebellion.
idiomatic: During the Wei era he rose from general who sweeps bandits to outside-military military assistant in the expeditionary office of Shuo Province, and followed Ge Rong in rebellion.

literal: When Ge was defeated, Erzhu Rong made him a commander.
idiomatic: When Ge was defeated, Erzhu Rong made him a commander.

literal: For merit in attacking Yuan Hao he was appointed Administrator of Ji Commandery.
idiomatic: For merit in attacking Yuan Hao he was appointed administrator of Ji Commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Jianming he was made envoy comforting the army on the eastern route, enfeoffed Viscount of Xingtang County with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianming he was made envoy comforting the army on the eastern route, enfeoffed viscount of Xingtang County with a fief of three hundred households.

literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the grand commandant.

literal: He went out as Administrator of Henei and was appointed Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Henei and was appointed governor of Ji Province.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao was defeated, he returned to the Grand Ancestor and was transferred to Governor of Fen Province.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao was defeated, he returned to Gao Huan and was transferred to governor of Fen Province.

literal: During Tianping, the Grand Ancestor seized Xia Province by surprise; Qiong was made envoy comforting the army and was left to garrison it.
idiomatic: During Tianping, Gao Huan seized Xia Province by surprise; Zhang Qiong was made envoy comforting the army and was left to garrison it.

literal: Soon afterward he was trapped by Emperor Wen of Zhou and died.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was trapped by Yuwen Tai and died.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yan, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, grand general, Duke over the Masses, and Governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yan, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, grand general, duke over the masses, and governor of Heng Province.

literal: He had two sons.
idiomatic: He had two sons.

literal: The eldest was Xin, the second Zunye.
idiomatic: The eldest was Xin, the second Zunye.

literal: Xin, during Putai, was made a commander and followed Erzhu Shilong.
idiomatic: Xin, during Putai, was made a commander and followed Erzhu Shilong.

literal: For merit he married the Princess of Pingyang of Wei, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse-guarding Consorts, Grand General, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, Governor of Jian Province, and Baron of Nanzheng County.
idiomatic: For merit he married the Princess of Pingyang of Wei, and was appointed commandant of the horse-guarding consorts, grand general, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, governor of Jian Province, and baron of Nanzheng County.

literal: Qiong often worried that his rank was too high; he would tell close friends and acquaintances, "For any man, in office and rank nothing is better than holding the middle; Xin's rank is too high — I am deeply anxious about it.
idiomatic: Zhang Qiong often worried that his rank was too high; he would tell close friends and acquaintances, "For any man, in office and rank nothing is better than holding the middle; Xin's rank is too high — I am deeply anxious about it.

literal: " But Xin was arrogant, dangerous, and unrestrained; he soon fell out with the princess, and was shortly killed by Emperor Wu — at the time people praised Qiong's foresight.
idiomatic: " But Xin was arrogant, dangerous, and unrestrained; he soon fell out with the princess, and was shortly killed by Emperor Wu of Wei — at the time people praised Zhang Qiong's foresight.

literal: Zhang Zunye
idiomatic: Zhang Zunye

literal: Zunye, for merit in attacking Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed Establishing-the-State Viscount of Gu'an County, and appointed General of Tranquil Distance and Grand Rectifier of Yun Province.
idiomatic: Zunye, for merit in attacking Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed establishing-the-state viscount of Gu'an County, and appointed general of tranquil distance and grand rectifier of Yun Province.

literal: During Tianping he was appointed Administrator of Qinghe, and soon was additionally made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jian Province.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was appointed administrator of Qinghe, and soon was additionally made general who pacifies the west and governor of Jian Province.

literal: During Wuding he followed Equal in Protocol Liu Feng in attacking Hou Jing, and was captured by Jing.
idiomatic: During Wuding he followed Equal in Protocol Liu Feng in attacking Hou Jing, and was captured by Jing.

literal: When Jing was defeated, he killed Zunye at Woyang.
idiomatic: When Jing was defeated, he killed Zunye at Woyang.

literal: When the coffin returned, Shizong came in person to mourn; posthumously granted command of military affairs in the four provinces of Bing, Si, You, and An, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: When the coffin returned, Gao Cheng came in person to mourn; posthumously he was granted command of military affairs in the four provinces of Bing, Si, You, and An, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Bing Province.

literal: Hulu Qiangju
idiomatic: Hulu Qiangju

literal: Hulu Qiangju was a native of Tai'an.
idiomatic: Hulu Qiangju was a native of Tai'an.

literal: For generations his family were chieftains of the tribe.
idiomatic: For generations his family were chieftains of the tribe.

literal: His father Jin served in Wei as General of Flying Cavalry and commandant of Wuchuan garrison.
idiomatic: His father Jin served in Wei as general of flying cavalry and commandant of Wuchuan garrison.

literal: Qiangju in youth was fierce and resolute, with courage and strength.
idiomatic: Qiangju in youth was fierce and resolute, with courage and strength.

literal: During Yong'an he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, distinguished himself in battle, won Zhao's particular favor, and was constantly sent on campaigns.
idiomatic: During Yong'an he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, distinguished himself in battle, won Zhao's particular favor, and was constantly sent on campaigns.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor defeated Zhao, only then did he pledge genuine allegiance.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan defeated Zhao, only then did he pledge genuine allegiance.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, because he had been loyal to whom he served, also praised and rewarded him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, because he had been loyal to whom he served, also praised and rewarded him.

literal: During Tianping he was appointed Grand Commander and ordered to lead three thousand infantry and cavalry to guide the army in a surprise western strike against Xia Province, which they captured.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was appointed grand commander and ordered to lead three thousand infantry and cavalry to guide the army in a surprise western strike against Xia Province, which they captured.

literal: Later he accompanied the Grand Ancestor on the western campaign; when the main host forded the river, the generals gathered to debate their line of advance.
idiomatic: Later he accompanied Gao Huan on the western campaign; when the main host forded the river, the generals gathered to debate their line of advance.

literal: Qiangju said: "Black Badger has gathered a band of villains; their relative strength is known. If they seek only to hold fast, they have no grain or support to rely on.
idiomatic: Qiangju said: "Yuwen Tai has gathered a band of villains; their relative strength is known. If they seek only to hold fast, they have no grain or support to rely on.

literal: Now judging their state of mind, they are already like cornered beasts. If we do not give battle but press straight toward Xianyang, Xianyang stands empty and can be taken without fighting.
idiomatic: Now judging their state of mind, they are already like cornered beasts. If we do not give battle but press straight toward Xianyang, Xianyang stands empty and can be taken without fighting.

literal: Strike at the root, and they will have nowhere to return — then Black Badger's head can hang at the army gate.
idiomatic: Strike at the root, and they will have nowhere to return — then Yuwen Tai's head can hang at the army gate.

literal: " The generals disputed the plan, so they fought at the bend of the Wei and the main army suffered a great defeat.
idiomatic: " The generals disputed the plan, so they fought at the bend of the Wei and the main army suffered a great defeat.

literal: At the end of Tianping, Zhang Jian of Yingchuan gathered a crowd in rebellion and coordinated with the west through the passes; Qiangju followed commanders Hou Jing, Gao Ang, and others to attack and defeat them.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianping, Zhang Jian of Yingchuan gathered a crowd in rebellion and coordinated with the west through the passes; Qiangju followed commanders Hou Jing, Gao Ang, and others to attack and defeat them.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was appointed Governor of Qing Province and enfeoffed Marquis of Mi County.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was appointed governor of Qing Province and enfeoffed marquis of Mi County.

literal: At the beginning of Xinghe, the Grand Ancestor made him Grand Commander of the Central Army and soon transferred him to Governor of Dongxia Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xinghe, Gao Huan made him grand commander of the central army and soon transferred him to governor of Dongxia Province.

literal: The Grand Ancestor wished to win over distant tribes, so he had Qiangju go as envoy to the Azhiluo people to proclaim majesty and virtue; he pleased his superiors repeatedly and was greatly valued.
idiomatic: Gao Huan wished to win over distant tribes, so he had Qiangju go as envoy to the Azhiluo people to proclaim majesty and virtue; he pleased his superiors repeatedly and was greatly valued.

literal: He died in the province at thirty-six.
idiomatic: He died in the province at thirty-six.

literal: The Grand Ancestor mourned him deeply.
idiomatic: Gao Huan mourned him deeply.

literal: Posthumously granted command of military affairs in Bing and Heng provinces and Governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted command of military affairs in Bing and Heng provinces and governor of Heng Province.

literal: Hulu Xiaoging
idiomatic: Hulu Xiaoging

literal: His son Xiaoging from youth was intelligent, perceptive, and dignified, and repeatedly held prominent posts.
idiomatic: His son Xiaoging from youth was intelligent, perceptive, and dignified, and repeatedly held prominent posts.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, enfeoffed Prince of Yining, managed the inner court, and controlled the secrets of external and cavalry forces.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, enfeoffed prince of Yining, managed the inner court, and controlled the secrets of external and cavalry forces.

literal: At that time court discipline daily fell into chaos and policy rested with scheming eunuchs.
idiomatic: At that time court discipline daily fell into chaos and policy rested with scheming eunuchs.

literal: After Zhao Yanshen died, among court nobles holding confidential posts only Xiaoging stood somewhat in the upright path and did not sink into greed and corruption.
idiomatic: After Zhao Yanshen died, among court nobles holding confidential posts only Xiaoging stood somewhat in the upright path and did not sink into greed and corruption.

literal: When the Later Lord reached Qizhou he made Xiaoging Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When the Later Lord reached Qizhou he made Xiaoging director of the masters of writing.

literal: He also appointed Palace Attendant Secretariat member Xue Daohang as palace attendant and enfeoffed him Prince of Beihai.
idiomatic: He also appointed palace attendant secretariat member Xue Daohang as palace attendant and enfeoffed him prince of Beihai.

literal: The two urged the Later Lord to draw up the Chengguang Sovereign decree abdicating in favor of the Prince of Rencheng, and had Xiaoging carry the decree documents and the imperial seal to Ying Province.
idiomatic: The two urged the Later Lord to draw up the Chengguang Sovereign decree abdicating in favor of the Prince of Rencheng, and had Xiaoging carry the decree documents and the imperial seal to Ying Province.

literal: Xiaoging instead went straight to Ye, submitted to Emperor Wu of Zhou, and followed him into Chang'an, where he was given the rank of superior presenter.
idiomatic: Xiaoging instead went straight to Ye, submitted to Emperor Wu of Zhou, and followed him into Chang'an, where he was given the rank of superior presenter.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he rose to Grand Minister of the Treasury and died while serving as Minister of the People.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he rose to grand minister of the treasury and died while serving as minister of the people.

literal: Liu Shiqing
idiomatic: Liu Shiqing

literal: Liu Shiqing of Dai — his grandfather Ba served in Wei as Governor of Yan Province;
idiomatic: Liu Shiqing of Dai — his grandfather Ba served in Wei as governor of Yan Province;

literal: his father Wei held the position of Grand Master of Golden Crown and Purple Radiance.
idiomatic: his father Wei held the position of grand master of golden crown and purple radiance.

literal: Shiqing at the end of Wuping was palace attendant and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, with appointment and favor nearly matching Xiaoging's.
idiomatic: Shiqing at the end of Wuping was palace attendant and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, with appointment and favor nearly matching Xiaoging's.

literal: His disposition was very upright, his conduct cautious and meticulous, exceeding Xiaoging in these respects.
idiomatic: His disposition was very upright, his conduct cautious and meticulous, exceeding Xiaoging in these respects.

literal: He could speak the languages of the four barbarian peoples and ranked first in the age.
idiomatic: He could speak the languages of the four barbarian peoples and ranked first in the age.

literal: The Later Lord ordered him to translate the Nirvana Sutra into Turkic to present to the Turk khagan, and commanded Palace Attendant Secretariat member Li Delin to write its preface.
idiomatic: The Later Lord ordered him to translate the Nirvana Sutra into Turkic to present to the Turk khagan, and commanded palace attendant secretariat member Li Delin to write its preface.

literal: Shiqing died in the Kaihuang era of Sui while holding the rank of opener of a government office and personal guard flying-cavalry general.
idiomatic: Shiqing died in the Kaihuang era of Sui while holding the rank of opener of a government office and personal guard flying-cavalry general.

literal: Yao Xiong, styled Xiuwu, was a native of Changzi in Shangdang.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong, styled Xiuwu, was a native of Changzi in Shangdang.

literal: His grandfather Xuan served in Wei as Minister of Agriculture.
idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan served in Wei as minister of agriculture.

literal: His father Rong was an outside-section member of the Secretariat; Xiong in youth was fierce and resolute, skilled in mounted archery, and lightly valued wealth while heavily valuing integrity, winning esteem among his peers.
idiomatic: His father Rong was an outside-section member of the secretariat; Yao Xiong in youth was fierce and resolute, skilled in mounted archery, lightly valued wealth while heavily valuing integrity, and won esteem among his peers.

literal: During Yong'an he was appointed General Who Proclaims Military Might, attendant at the court, bearer of the staff sent to comfort and encourage the three provinces of Heng, Yan, and Shuo, and was then made a commander to follow Chilie Yan in suppressing Liu Lingzhu.
idiomatic: During Yong'an he was appointed general who proclaims military might, attendant at the court, bearer of the staff sent to comfort and encourage the three provinces of Heng, Yan, and Shuo, and was then made a commander to follow Chilie Yan in suppressing Liu Lingzhu.

literal: When that was pacified he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Yan Province, enfeoffed Baron of Chengping County with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: When that was pacified he was appointed general who pacifies the east, governor of Yan Province, enfeoffed baron of Chengping County with a fief of five hundred households.

literal: When the banner of righteousness was first raised, Xiong followed Erzhu Zhao in defeat at Guang'a, then led his forces to hold Ding Province and return to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: When the banner of righteousness was first raised, Yao Xiong followed Erzhu Zhao in defeat at Guang'a, then led his forces to hold Ding Province and return to Gao Huan.

literal: At the time his elder cousin's son Jie, whom Erzhu Zhao had appointed Governor of Cang Province, reached Ying Province, learned of Zhao's defeat, and also sent envoys to submit and surrender.
idiomatic: At the time his elder cousin's son Jie, whom Erzhu Zhao had appointed governor of Cang Province, reached Ying Province, learned of Zhao's defeat, and also sent envoys to submit and surrender.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, because both brothers showed genuine good faith, kept Jie to administer Ying Province affairs and soon made Xiong General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of Ying Province in place of Jie, advancing his rank to Duke and increasing his fief by five hundred households.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, because both brothers showed genuine good faith, kept Jie to administer Ying Province affairs and soon made Yao Xiong general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Ying Province in place of Jie, advancing his rank to duke and increasing his fief by five hundred households.

literal: At the time restraints on the law were lax, and officials gathered wealth from one another, but Xiong took only what was proper; he could also treat subordinates with generous favor, and officials and commoners deeply attached themselves to him.
idiomatic: At the time restraints on the law were lax, and officials gathered wealth from one another, but Yao Xiong took only what was proper; he could also treat subordinates with generous favor, and officials and commoners deeply attached themselves to him.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei entered the Pass, Xiong served as Grand Commander and followed Gao Ang in defeating Heba Sheng at Rang city.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei entered the Pass, Yao Xiong served as grand commander and followed Gao Ang in defeating Heba Sheng at Rang city.

literal: He campaigned back and forth in the pacification of the three Jing regions and was then appointed area commander over the four provinces of Two Yu, Yang, and Ying, and Governor of Yu Province.
idiomatic: He campaigned back and forth in the pacification of the three Jing regions and was then appointed area commander over the four provinces of Two Yu, Yang, and Ying, and governor of Yu Province.

literal: Yuan Hongwei held Ying Province in rebellion; the commoner Zhao Jizong killed the Administrator of Yingchuan, Shao Zhao, seized Lekou, styled himself Governor of Yu Province, and responded to Hongwei in the north.
idiomatic: Yuan Hongwei held Ying Province in rebellion; the commoner Zhao Jizong killed the administrator of Yingchuan, Shao Zhao, seized Lekou, styled himself governor of Yu Province, and responded to Hongwei in the north.

literal: Xiong led troops to attack, and Jizong was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong led troops to attack, and Jizong was defeated and fled.

literal: Because Xiong had marched out, the people then pushed the city man Wang Chang to be governor, held the province, and invited Western Wei.
idiomatic: Because Yao Xiong had marched out, the people then pushed the city man Wang Chang to be governor, held the province, and invited Western Wei.

literal: Xiong again joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing to suppress and pacify them.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong again joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing to suppress and pacify them.

literal: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo raided and took Pingxiang city, harrying the province borders.
idiomatic: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo raided and took Pingxiang city, harrying the province borders.

literal: Xiong set an ambush and struck; Hongzhi, Dangbo, and others were captured alive and the booty was very great.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong set an ambush and struck; Hongzhi, Dangbo, and others were captured alive and the booty was very great.

literal: Liang Minister of the Si Province Chen Qingzhi again led troops to press the provincial city; Xiong rode out to fight, swept all before him, took two wounds, and his fighting spirit grew fiercer still. Qingzhi was defeated and abandoned his baggage train in flight.
idiomatic: Liang minister of the Si Province Chen Qingzhi again led troops to press the provincial city; Yao Xiong rode out to fight, swept all before him, took two wounds, and his fighting spirit grew fiercer still. Qingzhi was defeated and abandoned his baggage train in flight.

literal: Later when Qingzhi again besieged Southern Jing Province, Xiong said: "Baigou Mound is a key strongpoint on Liang's northern frontier; attacking it while it lies empty will surely succeed. If they hear of the danger, the siege of Jing will lift of itself — this is an opportunity that must not be lost.
idiomatic: Later when Qingzhi again besieged Southern Jing Province, Yao Xiong said: "Baigou Mound is a key strongpoint on Liang's northern frontier; attacking it while it lies empty will surely succeed. If they hear of the danger, the siege of Jing will lift of itself — this is an opportunity that must not be lost.

literal: " He then led troops to attack it, and Qingzhi indeed abandoned Jing Province and came.
idiomatic: " He then led troops to attack it, and Qingzhi indeed abandoned Jing Province and came.

literal: Before he arrived, Xiong had already taken the city, capturing Liang's garrison commander Gou Yuanguang and two thousand soldiers.
idiomatic: Before he arrived, Yao Xiong had already taken the city, capturing Liang's garrison commander Gou Yuanguang and two thousand soldiers.

literal: Liang installed Yuan Qinghe as King of Wei to harass the southern wall.
idiomatic: Liang installed Yuan Qinghe as King of Wei to harass the southern wall.

literal: Xiong led troops to attack and inflicted a great defeat on Qinghe at Nandun.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong led troops to attack and inflicted a great defeat on Qinghe at Nandun.

literal: Soon afterward he joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing in breaking Liang's Chucheng.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing in breaking Liang's Chucheng.

literal: The people of Yu Province memorialized, again requesting Xiong as governor, and he again administered Yu Province affairs.
idiomatic: The people of Yu Province memorialized, again requesting Yao Xiong as governor, and he again administered Yu Province affairs.

literal: Chief clerk of Ying Province He Ruo Hui seized Governor Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict ordered Xiong together with Guang Province Governor Zhao Yu, Yang Province Governor Shiyun Bao, and others each to command their provincial forces and cavalry, and with the mobile-office commander Ren Yanjing combine strength to attack.
idiomatic: Chief clerk of Ying Province He Ruo Hui seized Governor Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict ordered Yao Xiong together with Guang Province Governor Zhao Yu, Yang Province Governor Shiyun Bao, and others each to command their provincial forces and cavalry, and with the mobile-office commander Ren Yanjing combine strength to attack.

literal: Western Wei sent its general Yi Feng leading troops to reinforce them; Yanjing and the others fought and were defeated.
idiomatic: Western Wei sent its general Yi Feng leading troops to reinforce them; Ren Yanjing and the others fought and were defeated.

literal: Yu and Bao each returned to their own provinces, held the cities, and surrendered to the enemy.
idiomatic: Zhao Yu and Shiyun Bao each returned to their own provinces, held the cities, and surrendered to the enemy.

literal: Xiong gathered the scattered troops and held Daliang.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong gathered the scattered troops and held Daliang.

literal: Because of Yanjing's defeat, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent his right deputy chief minister Wei Xiaokuan and others to attack Yu Province.
idiomatic: Because of Ren Yanjing's defeat, Yuwen Tai sent his right deputy chief minister Wei Xiaokuan and others to attack Yu Province.

literal: Xiong's commanders Guo Chengbai and Cheng Duobao and others raised Yu Province and surrendered to the enemy, seized Governor Feng Yong together with his family and the wives and children of his subordinates, several thousand persons in all, and intended to send them to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong's commanders Guo Chengbai and Cheng Duobao and others raised Yu Province and surrendered to the enemy, seized Governor Feng Yong together with his family and the wives and children of his subordinates, several thousand persons in all, and intended to send them to Chang'an.

literal: At Lekou, Xiong's outside-military military assistant Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun and others, several dozen horsemen from Daliang, intercepted them on the way, cut down Duobao, and rescued Xiong's family and dependents, returning them to Daliang.
idiomatic: At Lekou, Yao Xiong's outside-military military assistant Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun and others, several dozen horsemen from Daliang, intercepted them on the way, cut down Duobao, and rescued Yao Xiong's family and dependents, returning them to Daliang.

literal: Western Wei made Chengbai Administrator of Yingchuan, and Xiong again joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing to attack him.
idiomatic: Western Wei made Chengbai administrator of Yingchuan, and Yao Xiong again joined the mobile-office commander Hou Jing to attack him.

literal: Xiong separately broke Lekou and captured Chengbai.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong separately broke Lekou and captured Chengbai.

literal: Advancing to attack Xuanhu, he drove off Western Wei governors Zhao Jizong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others.
idiomatic: Advancing to attack Xuanhu, he drove off Western Wei governors Zhao Jizong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others.

literal: Xiong was again put in charge of Yu Province affairs.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong was again put in charge of Yu Province affairs.

literal: Western Wei made Shiyun Bao Governor of Yang Province and had him hold Xiang city;
idiomatic: Western Wei made Shiyun Bao governor of Yang Province and had him hold Xiang city;
